svg.data-port-modes-qsfp28: 40GE, 50GE and 100GE; DAC breakout to 2 x 50GE, 4 x 25GE or 4 x 10GE
svg.data-port-modes-qsfp-dd: 400GE fabric interconnect to a COR580 (Ramon) spine
svg.data-cooling: 4+1 redundant hot-swappable fan modules, behind a carrier-grade air filter
svg.data-software: ONIE installer pre-loaded; open-source and commercial NOS options
svg.data-timing: Synchronous Ethernet, IEEE 1588v2 PTP, timing synchronization stack interfaces
svg.data-mgmt-ports: 1x RJ-45 RS-232 console, 1x RJ-45 10/100/1000BASE-T management, 2x RJ-45 PPS/ToD, 2x RJ-45 stacking-sync, 2x SFP+ 10G out-of-band, 1x USB 2.0 Type-A, 1x micro-USB console, 1x 1PPS/10MHz coaxial
svg.data-emc: CE Mark, FCC Title 47 Part 15 Subpart B Class A, VCCI Class A
svg.data-nebs: GR-63-CORE, GR-1089-CORE (NEBS Level 3). The datasheet footnotes this line '* Pre-test. Certificate is by request with fees', so it is a pre-test claim and not a certification.

America"}},"power":"ac"},"dc-f2b":{"component-attrs":{"cor550-psu-ac":{"inlet":"dc-terminal","input":"dc"}},"description":"Dual 48 VDC supplies (datasheet: input 40 to 72 VDC; the quick start wires -48 to -60 VDC on #10 AWG) and the same five front-to-back fan trays - the datasheet's one DC ordering row. DRAWN WITH THE AC SUPPLY'S FACE, C14 inlet and all, because neither document pictures the DC unit: the build is real and orderable, and what it is fed with is a field a tool filters on, so it is declared rather than left out, and the wrong connector is the dc-supply-face gap.","kind":"orderable","part-numbers":{"7926-40XKFB-O-48V-F":{"part":"FNPZZ7640003A","power-cord":"none"}},"power":"dc"}},"datasheet":{"sha256":"e7a8daad0460fa5fc07d66a2d73f67861ace2fb1e82241bcf08683742d29410b","title":"Edgecore COR550 (AS7926-40XKFB) Core Router data sheet"},"description":"40x 100G QSFP28 and 13x 400G QSFP-DD 2RU cell-based core router (vendor alias AS7926-40XKFB), Broadcom BCM88690 Jericho2 with a BCM16K external TCAM and an Intel Xeon D-1548, ONIE-preloaded. Every port is on the front, along with a carrier-grade air filter that covers most of the faceplate that is not a cage; two AC supplies stack in one column at the left of the rear and five 4+1 fan trays fill the rest of it, front-to-back only.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"WHICH OF A QSFP28 PORT'S THREE LAMPS SHOWS WHICH BREAKOUT LANE. The quick start guide's Status LEDs panel states colours by SPEED and not by lamp - 'QSFP28 Port LEDs: Blue - 100G, Yellow - 40G, Cyan - 2 x 50G, Magenta - 4 x 25G, Green - 4 x 10G' - and never says how many lamps a port has, let alone what each one means. The face draws three, and a 4 x 25G or 4 x 10G breakout has four lanes, so the obvious one-lamp-per-lane reading cannot be right. The lamps carry the library's off/on default and no legend is invented. A LED table naming the lamps, or a bench photograph of one port under a known breakout, settles it.","what":"lane-lamp-legend"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"WHICH FABRIC PORT EACH LAMP OF A BLOCK'S TWO-LAMP COLUMN BELONGS TO. Each fabric block carries a vertical pair of lamps at its inboard edge, one pair per row, serving that row's two ports. Nothing in either document says which lamp is which port, and at 2.27 px/mm the lamps are 2 px across with no legend beside them. Each pair is therefore drawn `for:` BOTH of its ports rather than one lamp being assigned to each, because assigning them would be a guess wearing a measurement's clothes. A photograph of the fabric block at 5+ px/mm settles it.","what":"fabric-lamp-pairing"},{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["front"],"wanted":"THE OUTLINE OF EACH AIR-FILTER COVER AND THE POSITIONS OF ITS CAPTIVE SCREWS. The filter is a real field-replaceable assembly - the guide gives it a three-step procedure: loosen the cover's captive screws, swap the old filter for a new one, then refit the cover and tighten the captive screws - and the Overview numbers it as item 3. What is NOT resolvable is where one cover ends and the next begins: the mesh WINDOWS measure cleanly but a cover's own edge is a shadow line a pixel wide, and the screw heads sit in the top strip where the filter media's texture defeats every threshold that finds a smooth disc elsewhere on the face. The filters are therefore drawn as the vent fields they present rather than as seated FRU components. A mechanical drawing, or a straight-on photograph of the front at 5+ px/mm, would settle it.","what":"air-filter-cover"},{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"THE FACEPLATE OF THE 48 VDC SUPPLY. The datasheet offers '48 VDC Power Supply: Input Voltage: 40 to 72 VDC' beside the AC one, but both staged documents draw and photograph only the AC machine - the guide's Overview calls out '8. 2 x AC PSUs' and both rear elevations show C14 inlets. There is no DC face to model, so no cor550-psu-dc part was written, and the dc-f2b configuration seats the AC part - wrong at the connector, which is what this gap and lint L120 keep in view until a DC face turns up.","what":"dc-supply-face"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"THE VENDOR ORDERING CODES FOR THE AC SUPPLY AND THE FAN TRAY. The datasheet's ordering table lists chassis SKUs only (carried on the configurations), and the guide's replacement procedures name no part. Both FRUs are therefore named for the chassis, which library/components/README.md allows only because no model number exists to use instead. If a COR550 ordering table lands, both parts should be renamed to their FRUs and this device should take the major that costs - edgecore/fan-2u-1x1sn@1 is the precedent for both the rename and its price.","what":"psu-and-fan-ordering-codes"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"WHETHER EACH TRAY CARRIES ONE FAN OR TWO IN SERIES. The datasheet says '4+1 redundant, hot-swappable fan modules' and 'Fans: Hot-Swappable 4+1 redundant fans' and never gives a fan count. One rotor is visible through each tray's mesh. This vendor's other 2RU trays carry two in series and say so in words - edgecore/fan-2u-1x1sn@1's datasheets print '4 hot-swappable fan modules (2 fans per module), 8 fans total' - but nothing of the kind is printed for this machine, so the bay count is five and the fan count is not claimed.","what":"fans-per-tray"}],"groups":{"displays":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"Display"},"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"4+1","redundancy-note":"4+1 redundant, hot-swappable; five bays, and the vendor does not say how many fans a tray holds"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"description":"the rack ears and the product tag - things you neither connect to nor read.","index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster at the right-hand end of the faceplate - two SFP+ 10G out-of-band uplinks, a 1PPS/10MHz coaxial bulkhead, a USB-A service port, a micro-USB console, and six RJ-45s in three stacks carrying two stacking-sync ports, two PPS/ToD ports, the RS-232 console and the 1000BASE-T management port. Six media, one job; the vendor draws them as one cluster under one set of legends and so do we.","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-lamps":{"index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 redundant, load-sharing, hot-swappable"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp28-100g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfpdd-fabric":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"400g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"fabric","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Edgecore","maturity":"modelled","model":"COR550","name":"cor550","portfolio":{"family":"Core Router","line":"Service Provider","series":"COR550"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"DATASHEET, 'Dimensions (WxDxH): 440 x 635 x 87 mm (17.32 x 25.0 x 3.43 in)' (cor550-datasheet/doc.md:102), corroborated in words by the Key Features line 'Compact design, 635 mm depth'. The quick start guide states no size at all, so unlike this library's other Edgecore routers there is no second reading of the triple - and the imperial conversion in the datasheet's own parenthesis is the only internal check: 440/25.4 = 17.32, 87/25.4 = 3.43, both exact, and 635/25.4 = 25.0. 440 IS THE BODY, not the ear-to-ear width. Both elevations' ink panels measure to it with the rack ears absent from the drawing, and the ears are placed outside it at the library's 14 mm, as the AGR560 and DCS520 do on this same 440 x 87 shell."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1, and the two documents split the work cleanly. THE QUICK START GUIDE SETS EVERY DIMENSION. Its front elevation (cor550-qsg page 1, native embedded image 1122 x 230) has an ink panel of 1109 x 219 px, an aspect of 5.0639 against 440/87 = 5.0575 - 0.13% - giving 2.5205 px/mm on x and 2.5172 on y, isotropic to the same 0.13%. Its rear (1123 x 233 native, panel 1114 x 220) reads 5.0636, 0.12% out. The datasheet's own elevations are 1000 px wide against the guide's 1122 AND 1.30% out on aspect (front) and 0.9-2.2% (rear), so they lose on both counts. 0.13% IS TIGHT ENOUGH TO SAY THE INK BOX IS THE BODY BOX, which matters because every number below is scaled by that assumption. A uniform border of b pixels moves the aspect by about b x 0.73% on a box this shape - twice the reciprocal of the short side less twice that of the long one - so the 0.13% observed puts the border at about a FIFTH of a pixel. A shadow or a stroke wide enough to matter would have shown up as an aspect error and did not. ORTHOGRAPHIC, AND TESTED THE WAY THAT WORD DESERVES. The aspect check passes on perspective renders - this library has three EPS20x devices where it did - so the front's ganged columns were fitted as x_i = first + pitch*i + gutter*(i//2) on all four port rows and then refitted with a quadratic. The left bank of six fits to 0.084 mm rms and the quadratic term implies +0.09% across the row; the fabric rows fit to 0.05-0.10 mm and -0.09 to -0.18%. Nothing is bent. The rear's five fan frames fit a straight line to 0.37 mm rms - under one pixel - with a quadratic worth 0.03 mm. THE REAR LOOKED LIKE A PERSPECTIVE RENDER FOR AN HOUR AND WAS NOT. Segmenting the red fan handles on red-channel BRIGHTNESS made them widen monotonically across the row, 4.74 to 11.85 mm for five identical parts, which is what a perspective render does. It is the lighting: the rear is lit from the right and the same curved handle passes a brightness threshold over more of itself the further right it sits. Re-segmenting on the chroma fraction (R - max(G,B))/(R+G+B), which does not care how brightly a part is lit, the trend disappears. The frames, not the handles, are what the pitch is fitted on above. THE DATASHEET IS STILL THE ONLY WITNESS TO SOME THINGS, and where it is, that is said at the point of use: the per-port lamps exist only in its render, because the guide's line art draws the legend strip empty."},"port-pitch":{"confidence":"registry","note":"THE REGISTRY'S 19.0 IS CARRIED, AND THE FIGURE CANNOT TELL IT FROM WHAT IT MEASURES. Fitting the guide's front with the pitch free gives 19.2426 +/- 0.097 on the left bank and 19.1434 +/- 0.099 on the right; the datasheet's independent artwork gives 19.1592 and 19.0490. Pinning the pitch to the registry's 19.0 and refitting only the first column and the gutter costs a MAXIMUM residual of 0.237 mm on the left bank and 0.121 mm on the right - both under one pixel, which here is 0.397 mm. SO THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT RESOLVABLE AND THE MEASURED GEOMETRY WINS. standards.yaml's qsfp-ganged pitch is 19.000 measured off TE 2322551-4's two openings at 96.750 and 115.750, a real cage part; 19.24 is a fit to a 2.5 px/mm drawing. Every other Edgecore ganged-QSFP block in this library takes `pitch: registry` for the same reason, so this device is not the one to break the convention on a fifth of a pixel. THE APERTURE WIDTH IS AN INDEPENDENT CHECK ON THE SCALE, and it passes. The drawn dark opening averages 18.58 mm against the registry's 18.50 cage opening - 0.4% - so the 440 mm assumption that sets px/mm is not carrying a systematic error big enough to explain the pitch gap. Its HEIGHT does not check out the same way (8.73 drawn against 9.58) and is not used: the cages are drawn with the module's own light latch-line across them, which truncates the dark region vertically but not horizontally. THE GUTTERS ARE MEASURED, because the registry says nothing about them. 4.70 mm between the 100G gangs on the left bank and 4.75 on the right - two independent fits agreeing to 0.05 mm is itself the evidence that the two banks are the same hardware - and 7.13 between the fabric gangs."},"rows":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED on the guide's front. The four 100G port rows' apertures top at 20.66, 36.15, 51.25 and 66.74 mm, so the two rows WITHIN a block sit 15.49 apart and the gap between the two block-rows is 15.10 - the smaller of the two, which is not what a first look expects, because the second block-row's numerals are printed in it. The fabric rows top at 36.15 and 50.85, a 14.70 row pitch, and the upper fabric row's aperture centres land at the same 40.52 mm as the 100G row below the numerals: one more cross-check that costs nothing and would have caught a transposed row. THE LOWER BLOCK-ROW READS ONE PIXEL RIGHT OF THE UPPER, consistently, across all twelve columns. 0.40 mm is below what this figure resolves and both block-rows are modelled on the same x; it is written down because a systematic one-pixel offset is the kind of thing that is either an artefact or a real 0.4 mm and this figure cannot say which."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"Two documents, both docling-converted, and they are NOT of equal standing here - see figure-choice. cor550-datasheet (the COR550 / AS7926-40XKFB data sheet) carries the spec list, the thirteen-callout Interfaces table and, on page 2, a rendered front and rear elevation in colour. cor550-qsg (the AS7926-40XKFB quick start guide) carries a line-art front and rear elevation on page 1, the Overview callouts, the Status LEDs panel and the FRU replacement procedures. Both letter the artwork AS7926-40XKFB, which is this device's own vendor alias, so the figure/product check passes. THE GUIDE IS TWELVE PAGES THAT ARE FOUR. Pages 1-4, 5-8 and 9-12 carry the same embedded images, so the document is one four-page guide printed three times; every figure cited below is from the first copy. It also carries this vendor's standard disclaimer, \"The switch drawings in this document are for illustration only and may not match your particular switch model\" - which is why every number here was checked against the datasheet's independent artwork rather than taken on the guide's word. Three product photographs are staged (cor550-1/-2/-3) at 489 x 357 px. They are too small to measure - 1.1 px/mm on a 440 mm face - and were used only to confirm the arrangement of the front, which they do."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 1 SFP pair (oob-0/oob-1), the 20 QSFP pairs (port-0/port-1 to port-38/port-39), the 6 QSFP-DD pairs (fab-0/fab-1 to fab-10/fab-11). 26 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic bail-outward."},"the-face-is-forty-plus-thirteen":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED, and the count agrees with the datasheet's words three ways over. THE 100G PORTS ARE IN FOUR BLOCKS OF TWO ROWS. Threshold-and-label over the guide's front finds 53 cage apertures of 47 x 22 px; twenty-four of them fall in a left bank of six columns and sixteen in a right bank of four, each bank two ports deep and drawn twice over (rows 0/1 numbered 0-19, rows 2/3 numbered 20-39). The silkscreen confirms the numbering directly: 0/1, 2/3 ... 10/11 over the left bank's upper rows, 12/13 ... 18/19 over the right bank's, 20-31 and 32-39 over the lower ones. Forty, against the datasheet's '40 x 100G QSFP28 ports'. THE 400G FABRIC PORTS ARE THIRTEEN AND THE THIRTEENTH IS ON ITS OWN. The middle carries seven cages in the upper row and six in the lower, silkscreened FAB 0, FAB 2 ... FAB 12 above and FAB 1, FAB 3 ... FAB 11 below - column-major, evens on top. The first twelve sit on one lattice; FAB 12's aperture centre reads 279.08 where a fourth gang of that lattice would put it at 280.19, so it is modelled as its own block rather than forced onto a pitch it is 1.1 mm off."},"the-filters-are-drawn-as-what-they-present":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE MESH IS MEASURED AND THE COVER IS NOT, and the difference is why these are decor rather than seated parts - see the gap. Variance-thresholding the guide's front (the filter media reads a local variance of 300-400 against the plain panel's 1) finds the windows cleanly: three across the top left at [13.1, 3.6], [49.6, 3.6] and [87.3, 3.6], about 35 x 11 each; three TALLER ones across the top middle, about 48 x 27 from x 135.5; three more across the top right at [298.8, 4.4], [331.7, 4.4] and [365.8, 4.8], about 30 x 9; an L-shaped field above the management cluster at [402.7, 4.8], 32 x 20; and three along the bottom middle at y 67.1, about 41-44 x 16. THE DRAWN TEXTURE IS A STAND-IN AND THE WEAVE IS NOT MEASURABLE. Autocorrelating the media across a window of the top-middle field gives a strongest peak at 1.19 mm (r=0.23) on the quick start guide and scattered peaks at 1.76, 3.96, 5.29 and 7.05 mm on the datasheet, which agree on nothing; pixel-to-pixel correlation is 0.29 and 0.38, barely above white noise. The weave is finer than either figure resolves. So the fields are drawn with `pattern: holes` at a 1.60 x 1.50 pitch - fine perforation, legible at render scale, and NOT a reading. The library's fixed `vent` honeycomb was the first choice and is wrong here in a way worth recording: its cell is 8.86 mm, which would have asserted a coarse hex grille where both documents show something too fine to resolve at 2.5 px/mm. THE FIRST PASS FOUND ALMOST NONE OF THEM. The variance threshold was set at 700 from a guess and the media's own variance is 300-400, so it returned four windows out of thirteen and two of those were the seven-segment display and an RJ-45's hatching. The threshold was then taken from the media rather than from the air."},"the-lamps-are-three-per-port-and-only-one-document-draws-them":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THE QUICK START GUIDE DRAWS THE LEGEND STRIP EMPTY. Its front elevation is line art; the white band between each column's two ports carries no lamps at all. The lamps exist only in the datasheet's rendered front - the figure this model does NOT trust for dimensions - so their spacing is quoted from the weaker instrument and says so. THREE PER PORT, and the arithmetic is in edgecore/cor550-lane-leds@1's provenance at length: twelve dots per four-port block, in four groups of three on a 2.70 mm pitch with a 4.19 mm step between groups, the group centres 9.59 apart - half the 19.0 column pitch. Four lamps at that pitch would span 8.1 mm and leave 1.5 mm between groups where 4.19 is measured, so four does not fit. WHICH LAMP MEANS WHICH LANE IS NOT PUBLISHED - see the gap."},"the-management-cluster":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED on the guide's front, at its own 2.52 px/mm, which is coarse for parts this small: one pixel is 0.397 mm and nothing in this cluster is good to better than about half a millimetre. Reading left to right and top to bottom as the face lays it out: the two 10G SFP+ out-of-band cages stacked at x 376.9 with their apertures at y 20.26 and 35.75 - a 15.49 row pitch, the same as the 100G rows and 0.49 off the registry's 15.0 for ganged SFP+; the 1PPS/10MHz coaxial bulkhead at [396.4, 36.6], 7.5 mm across, which common/smb-jack@1's 7.0 fits; the two-digit seven-segment display, its digits at [408.7, 31.4] and [416.6, 31.4] on a 7.93 pitch; the USB-A standing on end at [426.1, 4.4]; the four system lamps under the SYS/LOC, DIAG, PWR and FAN legends, whose text blobs centre at 404.3, 411.4, 416.4 and 421.2; the reset pinhole behind its RST legend; the micro-USB console at [425.7, 49.7]; and three RJ-45 stacks of two whose bright bezels read 16.66 x 25.03 at x 376.9, 397.2 and 417.8. THE LAMP ROW IS THE WEAKEST THING HERE. At this resolution the system lamps and their own legends are both 2-4 px tall and the thresholder cannot reliably tell one from the other; the lamps are placed under the legend centres, which is where the datasheet's render puts them, rather than from a reading of the lamps themselves."},"the-rear":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED on the guide's rear at 2.5318 px/mm and checked throughout against the datasheet's own, which is a different render of the same machine. THE SUPPLIES ARE A COLUMN OF TWO AT THE LEFT, not a pair at the two ends the way this shell's DCS520 seats them. Vertical-edge scans put the modules' flanges at 13.82 and 68.32 - 54.5 wide - and horizontal scans find exactly three bands down the faces: the top frame, the seam between the two modules at 42.3-45.9, and the bottom. The datasheet finds the same three within 0.9 mm. Taking the seam centre at 43.6 gives 40.8 per module at y 2.2 and 44.2. The chassis prints PSU1 above PSU0 on the web to their left, so the upper bay is 1. THE FIVE FAN TRAYS ARE ON A 68.53 PITCH from 84.45, fitted on their inboard frames to 0.37 mm rms, and 68.0 wide - the last tray's outboard frame reads 426.57 against a fitted left of 358.56. They are 62.3 tall between grille frames that both documents agree on, which leaves about 12 mm of chassis rail above and below; the FAN n legends are printed on the lower rail rather than on the trays. FAN 0 is at the outboard end and FAN 4 beside the supplies, so the numbering runs right to left. THE GROUND POINT is the strip between the supplies and the first tray, at about x 70, where both documents draw the earth symbol beside two fasteners."},"the-rj45s-are-five-bare-and-one-lamped":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THE DRAWING CANNOT ANSWER THIS AND THE WORDS CAN, which is the opposite of how this question usually goes. At 12x on the datasheet's render the six jacks show their eight-contact combs and their latch notches clearly and show NO LED windows in any housing corner - but a corner window at 2.27 px/mm is about one pixel, so absence there is not evidence. On the EPS112 the same question was settled by looking, at 11.9 px/mm; here that is not available. SO IT IS SETTLED BY WHAT THE VENDOR SAYS. The guide's Status LEDs panel gives 'Management Port LEDs: SFP+ OOB Port - Green (10G), Amber (1G); RJ-45 OOB Port - Right (link), Left (activity)' - lamps stated for the out-of-band Ethernet jack and for nothing else. The console RJ-45 is RS-232, and the stacking-sync and PPS/ToD jacks are timing, none of which the vendor gives lamps. That is also exactly L76's convention - an Ethernet RJ45 is a lamped part and a console or timing RJ45 is a bare one - so the census and the document agree. The top jack of the right-hand stack is the console and the bottom is MGMT: the guide's CONSOLE legend brackets the micro-USB and the upper jack together, which is the pair the datasheet lists as '7. 1 x Micro USB console port' and '8. 1 x RJ-45 console port', and MGMT is printed under the lower one."},"weight":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"DATASHEET, 'Weight: 39 kg (GW), 19 kg (NW)'.
